verses.en: Just then a prophet arrived from Judah with the Lord’s message for Bethel, as Jeroboam was standing near the altar ready to offer a sacrifice.
verses.ja: ちょうどその時、主の言葉を携えた一人の預言者がユダからベテルへやって来た。ヤロボアムが犠牲を献げようとして祭壇の傍らに立っていた時のことである。

verses.en: He cried out against the altar with the Lord’s message, “O altar, altar! This is what the Lord has said, ‘Look, a son named Josiah will be born to the Davidic dynasty. He will sacrifice on you the priests of the high places who offer sacrifices on you. Human bones will be burned on you.’”
verses.ja: 彼は主の言葉によって祭壇に向かって叫んだ。「祭壇よ、祭壇よ！ 主はこう言われる。『見よ、ダビデ家にヨシヤという名の息子が生まれる。彼はあなたの上で、高き所で犠牲を献げる祭壇の祭司たちを屠り、あなたの上で人間の骨を焼き払うであろう。』」

1.en: [翻訳注]  Heb “Look.” The Hebrew particle הִנֵּה (hinneh) is a rhetorical device by which the author invites the reader to visualize the scene for dramatic effect.
[翻訳注]  Heb “came by the word of the Lord to Bethel.”

2.en: [翻訳注]  Heb “by the word of the Lord.”
[解説]  ‘Look…you.’ For the fulfillment of this prophecy see 2 Kgs 23:15-20.

3.en: [翻訳注]  Heb “the fat.” Reference is made to burnt wood mixed with fat. See HALOT 234 s.v. דשׁן.

4.en: [翻訳注]  Heb “Jeroboam extended his hand from the altar.”
[翻訳注]  Heb “dried up” or “withered.” TEV and NLT interpret this as “became paralyzed.”

5.en: [翻訳注]  Heb “the fat.” Reference is made to burnt wood mixed with fat. See HALOT 234 s.v. דשׁן.
[翻訳注]  Heb “were poured out from the altar.”
[翻訳注]  Heb “according to the sign which the man of God had given by the word of the Lord.”

6.en: [翻訳注]  Heb “The king answered and said to.”
[翻訳注]  Heb “the man of God” (a second time later in this verse, and once in v. 7 and v. 8).
[翻訳注]  Heb “appeased the face of the Lord.”
[翻訳注]  Heb “and it was as in the beginning.”

8.en: [翻訳注]  Heb “eat food and drink water.”

9.en: [翻訳注]  Heb “for this he commanded me by the word of the Lord, saying.”
[翻訳注]  Heb “eat food and drink water.”

11.en: [地図]  For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.

[翻訳注]  Heb “and his son came and told him.” The MT has the singular here, but several other textual witnesses have the plural, which is more consistent with the second half of the verse and with vv. 12-13.
[翻訳注]  Heb “all the actions which the man of God performed that day in Bethel, the words which he spoke to the king, and they told them to their father.”

12.en: [翻訳注]  The Hebrew text has “and his sons saw” (וַיִּרְאוּ [vayyir’u], Qal from רָאָה [ra’ah]). In this case the verbal construction (vav consecutive + prefixed verbal form) would have to be understood as pluperfect, “his sons had seen.” Such uses of this construction are rare at best. Consequently many, following the lead of the ancient versions, prefer to emend the verbal form to a Hiphil with pronominal suffix (וַיַּרְאֻהוּ [vayyar’uhu], “and they showed him”).

16.en: [翻訳注]  Heb “I am unable to return with you or to go with you.”
[翻訳注]  Heb “eat food and drink water.”

17.en: [翻訳注]  Heb “for a word to me by the word of the Lord.”
[翻訳注]  Heb “eat food and drink water.”

18.en: [翻訳注]  Heb “and he said to him.”
[翻訳注]  Heb “by the word of the Lord.”
[翻訳注]  Heb “eat food and drink water.”

[翻訳注]  Or “deceiving him.”[解説]  He was lying to him. The motives and actions of the old prophet are difficult to understand. The old man’s response to the prophet’s death (see vv. 26-32) suggests he did not trick him with malicious intent. The old prophet probably wanted the honor of entertaining such a celebrity, or perhaps simply desired some social interaction with a fellow prophet.

19.en: [翻訳注]  Heb “and he returned with him and ate food in his house and drank water.”

20.en: [翻訳注]  Heb “and the word of the Lord came to the prophet who had brought him back.”

21.en: [翻訳注]  The Hebrew text has “because” at the beginning of the sentence. In the Hebrew text vv. 21-22 are one long sentence comprised of a causal clause giving the reason for divine punishment (vv. 21-22a) and the main clause announcing the punishment (v. 22b). The translation divides this lengthy sentence for stylistic reasons.
[翻訳注]  Heb “the mouth [i.e., command] of the Lord.”

22.en: [翻訳注]  Heb “and you returned and ate food and drank water in the place about which he said to you, ‘do not eat food and do not drink water.’”
[翻訳注]  “Therefore” is added for stylistic reasons. See the note at 1 Kgs 13:21 pertaining to the grammatical structure of vv. 21-22.
[翻訳注]  Heb “will not go to the tomb of your fathers.”

23.en: [翻訳注]  Heb “and after he had eaten food and after he had drunk.”
[翻訳注]  Heb “and he saddled for him the donkey, for the prophet whom he had brought back.”

24.en: [翻訳注]  Heb “and he went and a lion met him in the road and killed him.”
[翻訳注]  Heb “and his corpse fell on the road, and the donkey was standing beside it, and the lion was standing beside the corpse.”

25.en: [翻訳注]  Heb “Look, men were passing by.”
[翻訳注]  Heb “the corpse.” The noun has been replaced by the pronoun (“it”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.
[翻訳注]  The words “what they had seen” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

26.en: [翻訳注]  Heb “and the prophet who had brought him back from the road heard.”
[翻訳注]  Heb “the mouth of the Lord.”
[翻訳注]  Heb “according to the word of the Lord which he spoke to him.”

28.en: [翻訳注]  Heb “the corpse.” The noun has been replaced by the pronoun (“it”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.

29.en: [翻訳注]  Heb “the prophet.” The word “old” has been supplied in the translation to distinguish this individual from the other prophet.

30.en: [翻訳注]  “They” is the reading of the Hebrew text here; perhaps this is meant to include not only the old prophet but his sons (cf. v. 31).

32.en: [翻訳注]  Heb “for the word which he cried out by the word of the Lord”
[地図]  For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.

[翻訳注]  Heb “Samaria.” The name of Israel’s capital city here stands for the northern kingdom as a whole. Actually Samaria was not built and named until several years after this (see 1 Kgs 16:24), so it is likely that the author of Kings, writing at a later time, is here adapting the old prophet’s original statement.

33.en: [翻訳注]  Heb “did not turn from his evil way.”
[解説]  The expression common people refers to people who were not Levites. See 1 Kgs 12:31.
[翻訳注]  Heb “and one who had the desire he was filling his hand so that he became [one of] the priests of the high places.”
